messages:
samir: Heads-up — planning change: customers want a way to grant a "audit_reader" scoped token that can fetch audit events for their tenant but should not decrypt any KMS-wrapped payloads. How do we model visibility vs decryption?
elaine: Good call. We need two orthogonal controls: 1) RBAC for who can LIST/QUERY audit events, 2) KMS key policy / service proxy for DECRYPT. Audit readers should get redacted payloads if they don't have decrypt rights. :lock:
maria: From product pov, customers expect to see who did what but not internal secrets. We should define a customer-facing audit schema that marks sensitive fields as "sensitive": true and we automatically redact them unless the requester has decrypt rights.
kevin: Operationally, if we return redacted events to scoped tokens we avoid introducing another cross-tenant decryption surface. Suggest an intermediary "audit-proxy" service with a narrow KMS IAM role for decryption. Only org-level admins who opt-in can enable full events.
faye: Quick Q — what about existing export pipelines? If we change schema to add a new "redacted_fields" array, we need back-compat. Could we add a new top-level field: "redaction_profile": "minimal|strict|none"?
elaine: Yes additive-only fields are safest. Proposed minimum schema change: add "redacted_fields": [], "redaction_profile": "minimal" and keep existing fields identical. Also add a new metadata flag "requires_decrypt": true when payload was wrapped by KMS.
samir: Sample event for reference (we can paste in docs):
```
{
  "event_id": "evt_2026_0001",
  "tenant_id": "t-12345",
  "actor": {"id": "u-42", "role": "project_admin"},
  "action": "model.deploy",
  "resource": "model:m-abc",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-20T15:04:05Z",
  "outcome": "success",
  "payload": "<kms-wrapped-b64>",
  "requires_decrypt": true
}
```
kevin: That looks fine. For scoped tokens we should return the event with `payload` replaced by `null` and populate `redacted_fields": ["payload"]` and `redaction_profile": "minimal". If the caller has the audit_decrypt scope and the org has enabled decryption, the proxy can swap in the clear payload.
maria: UX question: customers will confuse "can see events" with "can see payloads". We should document roles clearly: member, audit_reader, audit_decrypt, org_admin. Default audit_reader = metadata-only.
faye: Edge case: what about cross-tenant support people who need to view customer audit logs during incident triage? We must ensure scoped tokens they use are tenant-scoped and logged. Maybe implement time-limited emergency decrypt tokens with additional approvals.
elaine: Agreed. Add an audit event every time decryption is performed by proxy: `action=\"audit.decrypt\" actor=service_account ... reason` — that creates an immutable trail. :white_check_mark:
audit-bot: SYSTEM: New schema proposal posted to #doc-registry at https://docs.internal/redwood/audit-schema/v2 (draft).
samir: For RBAC enforcement we can reuse our existing policies but need a check in the audit API: check principal has either tenant==event.tenant_id and role in [org_admin, audit_reader] OR has scope audit_decrypt and org opt-in. Keep the logic minimal.
kevin: Also consider pagination/CSV exports. Exports should obey the same redaction rules. If a user requests an export and has decrypt rights, we stream decrypted rows; otherwise stream redacted rows and include `redaction_profile` header.
maria: Action items: 1) security to write a formal policy for audit_reader vs audit_decrypt (elaine) 2) eng to implement `redacted_fields` + `requires_decrypt` (faye) 3) infra to build audit-proxy with KMS role and logging (kevin) 4) docs to update customer-facing table of roles (maria).
elaine: Assigning: I will draft the policy and incident review steps. Also adding requirement: any decryption must require a reason field and create an `audit.decrypt` event.
faye: I'll prototype the API changes this week. Will post a short PR with the schema addition and unit tests.
kevin: I'll spin up a small PoC audit-proxy that accepts signed service tokens and calls KMS on behalf of the proxy only. Will include a makefile and infra notes.
samir: Thanks all. One more thing — vuln triage: if a scoped token can be misissued, we need automated replay checks. Suggest adding a short-lived nonce on tokens used for audit access so we can correlate misuse.
elaine: Good point. Add token nonce to `audit.decrypt` event. That will help incident response.
maria: 👍 Can we add a short FAQ for customers about what they see in the UI vs exports? I'll draft after schema lands.
audit-bot: REMINDER: weekly security sync Tue 10am — please bring any PR links / schema diffs.
